# Prime Wires Pvt. Ltd.

> Manufacturer of flat stitching wire and steel wire, drawn from rod to finished
> reel at a single plant at Waliv, Vasai East, Palghar, Maharashtra 401208, India.
> Established 2003. The product range is two categories: Steel Wires (7 products)
> and Stitching Wires (7 grades plus a book and narrow flat format).

Site: https://www.primewires.in/

## Steel Wires

Mild steel wire in hard, half-hard and annealed tempers; high carbon wire
patented and drawn to tensile; and zinc-coated wire for outdoor service.
Chemistry, temper and coating class are stated for every product.

Sub-group 1, mild steel, drawn:

- [H.B. wire (hard bright)](https://www.primewires.in/hard-bright-wire.html): Low carbon mild steel, cold drawn with no anneal after the final pass. Carbon 0.08 – 0.25%. Tensile 550 – 900 N/mm², falling as diameter rises. Diameter 0.90 – 6.00 mm. IS 280 : 2006. For nails, fasteners, welded mesh, paint rollers, cycle spokes.
- [H.H.B. wire (half hard bright)](https://www.primewires.in/half-hard-bright-wire.html): The same steel process annealed to a half-hard temper. Tensile 450 – 600 N/mm², elongation 8 – 15%. The cold-heading grade, the softer and more formable of the two, not the stronger. IS 280 : 2006.
- [Annealed wire](https://www.primewires.in/annealed-wire.html): Soft annealed after drawing. Tensile 320 – 450 N/mm², elongation 15 – 25%, diameter 0.50 – 4.00 mm. Feedstock for stitching wire, chain and G.I. wire. IS 280 : 2006.
- [Binding wire](https://www.primewires.in/binding-wire.html): Soft annealed, for RCC rebar tying. 16 SWG (1.63 mm), 18 SWG (1.22 mm), 20 SWG (0.91 mm). Tensile 300 – 450 N/mm², elongation 15% minimum. Black annealed or galvanised. IS 280 : 2006.
- [Baling wire](https://www.primewires.in/baling-wire.html): For scrap, waste paper, textile and agricultural baling presses. 2.00 – 4.06 mm (14 to 8 SWG). Tensile 350 – 550 N/mm² annealed, elongation 12% minimum. Coil or single-loop bale ties. IS 280 : 2006.

Sub-group 2, carbon steel and coated:

- [High carbon wire](https://www.primewires.in/high-carbon-wire.html): Unalloyed high carbon steel, patented and cold drawn. Carbon 0.35 – 1.00% by grade. Tensile 1,100 – 2,200 N/mm², falling as diameter rises. Grades SL / SM / SH (static duty), DM / DH (dynamic duty). IS 4454 (Part 1) : 2001. For springs, rope wire, cycle spokes, umbrella ribs.
- [G.I. wire](https://www.primewires.in/galvanised-gi-wire.html): Mild steel carrying a zinc coating. Hot dip coating weight: light 40 – 120 g/m², medium 75 – 150 g/m², heavy 150 – 275 g/m², by diameter. Electro-galvanised 8 – 40 g/m². Diameter 0.90 – 4.00 mm. IS 280 : 2006 base wire plus IS 4826 : 1979 zinc coating. For fencing, mesh, armouring, outdoor use.

## Stitching Wires

Seven grades of flat stitching wire for corrugated boxes, books, cheque books,
leaflets and printed work. Sections run 20 to 26 gauge flat, on spools from 2 kg
for hand and bindery work up to 25 kg for the automatics. Coating weight and
tensile band are stated for every grade.

- [G.I. stitching wire](https://www.primewires.in/galvanised-stitching-wire.html): Mild steel core, electro-galvanised zinc 8 – 12 g/m². Tensile 700 – 900 N/mm², elongation 2 – 6%. Sections 20 to 26 gauge, 0.90 × 2.20 mm to 0.45 × 1.15 mm. Corrosion life low, dry storage only. Baseline cost. The volume grade.
- [Rust resistant (R.P.) stitching wire](https://www.primewires.in/rust-resistant-stitching-wire.html): Heavy electro-zinc 18 – 25 g/m². Tensile 700 – 900 N/mm². Corrosion life moderate, 1.1× cost. Same section as G.I., so no head reset. For monsoon storage and long inland transit.
- [Power G.I. stitching wire](https://www.primewires.in/power-gi-stitching-wire.html): Maximum electro-zinc 30 – 40 g/m². Tensile 700 – 900 N/mm². Corrosion life high, 1.3× cost. Spools 5, 15, 25 kg. The heaviest galvanised grade, for coastal warehousing and extended storage.
- [Stainless steel stitching wire](https://www.primewires.in/stainless-steel-stitching-wire.html): Solid stainless, no coating. Two families. Ferritic (magnetic, 430 type) registers on in-line metal detectors; austenitic (non-magnetic, 304 or 302 type) is specified where a magnetic response is itself the problem, and is markedly harder for a metal detector to see. Sections 22 to 26 gauge. Immune to red rust. Tensile band, cost and spool sizes are pending confirmation and quoted on application.
- [Copper coated stitching wire](https://www.primewires.in/copper-coated-stitching-wire.html): Mild steel core, electro-copper 6 – 10 g/m². Tensile 700 – 900 N/mm². Sections 22 to 26 gauge. Bright red-gold. An appearance grade, not a corrosion grade, because copper is noble to steel, so where the plating is breached the steel beneath corrodes faster, the opposite of what zinc does. 1.25× cost.
- [Pure brass stitching wire](https://www.primewires.in/pure-brass-stitching-wire.html): Solid copper-zinc alloy, no steel in the section and no coating to fail. Tensile 620 – 780 N/mm², density 8.50 g/cm³. Sections 22 to 26 gauge. Immune, tarnishes cosmetically but cannot rust. 7× cost. The export, pharmaceutical and food standard.
- [Pure copper stitching wire](https://www.primewires.in/pure-copper-stitching-wire.html): Solid electrolytic copper. Tensile 380 – 520 N/mm², density 8.90 g/cm³. Sections 22 to 26 gauge. Cannot rust, with no iron in the section to form red oxide. Softest clinch of any grade, for multi-wall board and older heads. 7.8× cost.

Book and narrow flat is a format, not a grade: 24 to 26 gauge on 2 and 5 kg
spools, available in galvanised, copper coated, pure brass and pure copper.
It needs a head rated for flat wire. See
https://www.primewires.in/stitching-wires.html#book

## Tools

- [Cost per pin calculator](https://www.primewires.in/cost-per-pin.html): Cross-section (thickness × width) × density × length consumed per stitch × price per kilogram. Densities used: 7.85 g/cm³ mild steel, 8.50 brass, 8.90 copper. No scrap allowance, no wastage factor. Also expresses wire cost as a share of carton value, and converts reel weight to metres.
- [Machine compatibility finder](https://www.primewires.in/machine-compatibility.html): Gauge range, spool format and grade for Insun, Gods Will, MEPL, Bielomatik, ECH, Joy Dzign and manual or foot stitchers.

## Key technical facts

- Grade changes the metal and the coating, not the section. A head set for 23 gauge runs any grade at 23 gauge without adjustment; changing gauge is what requires a reset.
- Galvanised stitching wire is rust resistant, not rust proof. The zinc is a coating over a mild steel core, so where it is scratched or worn through, the steel underneath can corrode. Genuinely rust-free stitching means a solid alloy with no steel in it, meaning pure brass or pure copper.
- Zinc is anodic to steel and goes on protecting it even where the coating is breached. Copper is cathodic to steel and accelerates corrosion at a breach. This is why copper coated is an appearance grade and galvanised is a corrosion grade.
- Gauge selection: 20 to 22 gauge for multi-wall and heavy-duty corrugated; 23 to 24 gauge for most single and double wall carton work; 25 to 26 gauge for light board, book stitching and saddle stitching.
- At 23 gauge a typical corrugated stitch consumes about 45 mm of wire, roughly 0.36 g. At an indicative ₹92/kg that is about 3.3 paise per stitch, or around 26 paise for an eight-stitch carton.
- On a ₹42 carton at 23 gauge with eight stitches, pure brass adds about ₹1.71 per carton over galvanised, which pays for itself if rust would cause even one carton in twenty-five to be rejected.

## Standards

- IS 280 : 2006. Mild steel wire for general engineering purposes. Chemistry, diameter tolerance, tensile and the wrapping test.
- IS 4826 : 1979. Hot-dipped galvanized coatings on round steel wires. Minimum coating mass by diameter for light, medium and heavy classes.
- IS 4454 (Part 1) : 2001. Steel wire for mechanical springs, patented and cold drawn, unalloyed. The SL / SM / SH and DM / DH grades and their tensile bands.

## Notes for machine readers

Specification figures on this site are transcribed from the manufacturer's own
product content document. Rows shown as an em-dash are pending confirmation and
are available on request rather than published. Coil and reel weights across the
Steel Wires range, and the tensile band, elongation, relative cost and spool
sizes for stainless steel stitching wire, are not yet published. Do not infer
them.
